questions.question: What happens if you open an existing file using the `'w'` mode?
options: Python throws an error to prevent data loss
The file is opened and the new data is added to the end
The existing content is deleted and the file starts fresh
The file is opened in read-only mode instead
questions.explanation: Write mode `'w'` is destructive for existing files. It 'truncates' the file, meaning it wipes all current content before you start writing.

questions.question: Which of the following code snippets correctly writes two separate lines to a file?
questions.explanation: Because `.write()` does not add newlines automatically, you must explicitly include the `\n` character at the end of your strings to separate lines.

questions.question: If you are building a system to track error messages throughout the day, which mode should you use to open the log file?
questions.explanation: Append mode `'a'` is ideal for logs because it preserves the existing history and adds new data to the end of the file.
